slides.texte_overlay:
Weekend habits of men
who get better every year
They wake up at roughly the same time. Not 5am, just not noon either. Keeping your body clock steady means Monday doesn't feel like jet lag every single week.
They do one physical challenge. A long hike, a new climbing route, a football match. Pushing your body at the weekend builds energy for the whole week ahead.
They see people in real life. Brunch with friends, a family lunch, a game with neighbours. Real connection on the weekend refills what the work week drains.
They learn something just for fun. I do five minutes of history, art or science every Saturday morning, and the weekend feels richer than any scrolling session.
slides.texte_sophia: Every Saturday morning I do five minutes on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. My weekend feels richer than any scrolling session.

slides.texte_overlay: They work on a personal project. A song, a garden, a side business, a bike. A couple of hours on something that's yours brings a deep kind of satisfaction.
They take care of the boring stuff early. Laundry, groceries, paying bills on Saturday morning. Then the rest of the weekend is free and guilt-free.
They switch off from work completely. No emails, no Slack, no checking in. Real rest is what lets them come back sharper, calmer and more creative on Monday.
